summary: Turkmenistan's State Migration Service says foreign citizens may enter and stay on the basis of a visa unless an international treaty of Turkmenistan provides otherwise. The UK Foreign Office says that on 1 October 2026 Turkmenistan introduced an e-visa for tourists and for people attending international conferences and exhibitions backed by its government: you cannot apply directly, your tour agency or event organiser acts as sponsor, and the e-visa replaces the letter of invitation followed by a visa in your passport. For any other purpose, it says, you still need a letter of invitation from a sponsoring organisation, and with it you apply at an Embassy of Turkmenistan or on arrival.

visaTypes.feeText: The UK Foreign Office says the cost of any visa depends on your length of stay in Turkmenistan and whether you apply for a single or multiple entry visa.

name.text: On 1 October 2026 Turkmenistan introduced an electronic (e-visa) system for tourists and people visiting to participate in international conferences and exhibitions backed by the Government of Turkmenistan.

method.text: You cannot apply for one of these visas directly. Your tour agency or event organiser will continue to act as a sponsor. However, when the visa is approved and paid for through your sponsor, you will receive an e-visa that can be printed off or presented electronically on arrival. The e-visa replaces the former two-part process of a letter of invitation followed by a visa vignette in your passport.

fee.notes: State Migration Service fee for an ordinary visa of up to one month; USD 20 for up to 10 days, USD 30 for up to 20 days, USD 30 for each further month. Multiple-entry visas: USD 60 for up to one month, USD 40 each further month. Children under 7 pay nothing and children 7–16 pay half; urgent processing within 3 working days doubles the fee. The UK government says that for any purpose other than tourism or conference participation you need a letter of invitation applied for on your behalf by a sponsoring organisation, and with it you can apply at your nearest Embassy of Turkmenistan or on arrival; Canada's travel advice says a letter of invitation must be presented in support of a visa application.

declarations.name: Migration fee and registration

fee.notes: Paid on arrival. The State Migration Service says children aged 7 to 16 pay 50% and children under 7 are exempt. The UK Foreign Office gives the migration fee as USD 14 and says a tourism tax of USD 2 per day of stay is charged separately, which hotels show as a separate item on the bill.

declarations.text: Turkmenistan's State Migration Service says foreign citizens and stateless persons arriving in or transiting Turkmenistan pay a registration fee of USD 10 for their stay; children aged 7 to 16 pay 50% and children under 7 are exempt. The UK government says the migration fee on arrival is USD 14, and that all foreign visitors also pay a tourism tax of USD 2 for each day of their stay. It says stays of more than 3 working days must be registered with the State Migration Service within 3 days of arrival, and that your hotel or sponsor will usually do this. Canada's travel advice says you must complete a migration card and pay a migration fee on arrival.

currencyLimits.text: Turkmenistan's customs service says foreign cash may be brought in without limit if it is declared to customs, and that you may take out up to USD 10,000 (or the equivalent), plus foreign cash you brought in and declared, on presenting the import declaration.

notes: The UK government says Turkmenistan's State Customs Service reports that you may enter with prescription medicines if you have a copy of the prescription with them, but that you could be prosecuted for possessing drugs Turkmenistan may classify as narcotics, such as morphine or strong painkillers, without a prescription or if carrying more than you need without declaring them on arrival.
The UK government says the tobacco allowance of 2 packs means, for example, 2 packets of cigarettes (40 cigarettes) or 2 cigars.

overstay.text: Under the Code of Administrative Offences, a foreigner who violates the rules of stay in Turkmenistan, including by living without a visa after it expires or evading departure after the permitted period, is fined eight to sixteen times the base amount, or administratively expelled with a temporary restriction on entry of up to five years.

postArrivalRegistration.penaltyText: Breaking the registration procedure: fine of eight to sixteen base units, or administrative expulsion with a temporary entry restriction of up to five years (Code of Administrative Offences, art. 383 part 1).
postArrivalRegistration.text: Foreign nationals must register with the migration service office at their place of stay within 3 working days after entering Turkmenistan, not counting the day of entry. Foreign nationals in transit whose stay does not exceed five days (not counting the day of entry) are registered only at the migration points of the border checkpoints. Breaking the registration procedure is punished by a fine of eight to sixteen base units, or by administrative expulsion with a temporary entry restriction of up to five years.

payments.text: The UK government says Turkmenistan is largely a cash-based society: carry cash and pay in manat; some larger hotels and restaurants accept US dollars (check before purchasing), while other outlets are only allowed to accept manat. It says you can exchange crisp, clean US dollar notes at the official rate at your hotel or a bank, that other currencies are difficult to exchange, that in Ashgabat a UK bank card can be used to withdraw or buy manat only at the State Bank for Foreign Economic Affairs, with a 3% withdrawal charge for each transaction, and that you are strongly recommended to bring enough dollars for your entire trip. The Government of Canada says a few hotels and restaurants in Ashgabat accept credit cards.

safety.text: The UK government says that while the crime rate is low you should exercise a similar level of caution as you would in the UK, that land border crossings can be subject to occasional and unannounced closures, that access to areas near the borders with Afghanistan and Iran is tightly restricted, and that although there is no recent history of terrorism in Turkmenistan, attacks cannot be ruled out.

tips.text: The UK government says visa applications that follow the letter-of-invitation process and are made through an Embassy of Turkmenistan are referred to Ashgabat for a decision, which can take up to a month unless a paid-for express service is available, and that a letter of invitation for a transit visa can take up to a month to issue.

The Government of Canada says photographing military installations, police stations, airports, government buildings and other sensitive sites may result in a penalty, and advises seeking permission from local authorities before taking photographs.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Turkmenistan?
faq.answer: Turkmenistan's State Migration Service says foreign citizens enter on the basis of a visa unless an international treaty of Turkmenistan provides otherwise. The UK Foreign Office says that on 1 October 2026 Turkmenistan introduced an e-visa for tourists and for people attending international conferences and exhibitions backed by its government; you cannot apply for it directly, your tour agency or event organiser acts as sponsor, and the e-visa can be printed off or presented electronically on arrival.

faq.question: How do I get a Turkmenistan letter of invitation?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says the letter comes from the person you will visit, the company you will work for or an authorised travel agency in Turkmenistan, which must submit a request to the State Migration Service. The UK government says that for tourists and conference visitors the e-visa introduced on 1 October 2026 replaces the letter of invitation followed by a visa in your passport; for any other purpose you still need a letter of invitation applied for on your behalf by a sponsoring organisation, and with it you can apply at your nearest Embassy of Turkmenistan, where the decision is referred to Ashgabat and can take up to a month unless a paid-for express service is available, or on arrival.

faq.question: Can I get a Turkmenistan visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Yes, with a letter of invitation, for visits for any purpose other than tourism or conference participation: the UK government says that once you have the letter you can apply for your visa on arrival, and that visas on arrival attract an additional fee of 50 US dollars. The State Migration Service charges a further USD 50 on top of the fee for a visa obtained at the international airport. For tourists and conference visitors, the UK government says the e-visa obtained through your sponsor can be printed off or presented electronically on arrival.

faq.question: Is there a Turkmenistan transit visa without an invitation letter?
faq.answer: No. The State Migration Service lists the transit visa for up to 5 days per trip. The UK government says you may be eligible for one if you will travel overland through Turkmenistan for fewer than 5 days and the purpose of your stay is transit rather than tourism; that the State Migration Service is the sole sponsor of transit visas; that you must secure the letter of invitation before you travel, which can take up to a month to issue, and it can then be converted to a transit visa at the land border checkpoint; that you must enter and leave through the border crossings specified in the letter of invitation; and that you cannot buy a transit visa at Baku seaport.

faq.question: Can I travel independently in Turkmenistan?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states whether tourists must be accompanied by a guide. Canada's travel advice says the areas bordering Iran, Uzbekistan and Afghanistan, including the city of Dashoguz and areas of the Caspian coast, are restricted zones that need permission from the Government of Turkmenistan, applied for at least 10 working days ahead. The UK government says transit-visa holders must enter and leave through the border crossings specified in the letter of invitation.

countryFacts.payments.text: Turkmenistan is largely a cash-based society. Carry cash and pay in the Turkmen currency, manat. Some larger hotels and restaurants accept US dollars - you should check before purchasing. Other outlets are only allowed to accept manat.
You can exchange US dollars at the official manat rate at your hotel or a bank. Bring crisp, clean notes as creased, damaged or marked notes will be rejected.
Other currencies are difficult to exchange.

It is possible in Ashgabat to use a UK bank card to withdraw manat from an ATM or buy manat over the counter, but only at the State Bank for Foreign Economic Affairs. There’s a 3% withdrawal charge for each transaction. You are strongly recommended to bring enough dollars for your entire trip.

countryFacts.safety.text: Whilst the crime rate is low, you should exercise a similar level of caution as you would in the UK.

Although there’s no recent history of terrorism in Turkmenistan, attacks cannot be ruled out.
